question: Buddhist texts called Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa, which are the sources of information to Mauryan times, belong to which of the following countries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Dipavamsa** and **Mahavamsa** are ancient Buddhist texts written in Pali.
 
• These texts are considered the earliest historical records of Sri Lanka.
 
• The Mahavamsa was composed in the 5th century AD, while the Dipavamsa predates it, being compiled in the 4th century AD.
 
• Both texts provide detailed accounts of the history of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, as well as the island's political and cultural history.
 
• These chronicles are essential sources of historical information about the reign of the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka and his role in the spread of Buddhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dipavamsa**

 
 
• The Dipavamsa, meaning "Chronicle of the Island," is the earliest extant chronicle of Sri Lanka.
 
• It provides accounts of the early history of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, including the arrival of Buddhism on the island.
 
• The text is believed to have been compiled by Buddhist monks of the Mahavihara tradition.
 
• It serves as a precursor to the more comprehensive Mahavamsa.
 
 
 
• **Mahavamsa**
 
 
• The Mahavamsa, meaning "Great Chronicle," was composed by the Buddhist monk Mahanama in the 5th century AD.
 
• This chronicle covers the history of Sri Lanka from the legendary past up to the reign of King Mahasena (334-361 AD).
 
• The Mahavamsa is divided into three parts: the Mahavamsa, the Culavamsa, and the modern continuation of the chronicle.
 
• It is considered a vital source for understanding the historical and cultural development of Sri Lanka.
 
 
 
• **Role of Emperor Ashoka**
 
 
• Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Dynasty played a crucial role in the spread of Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
 
• He sent his son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitta to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhist teachings.
 
• The Mahavamsa provides detailed accounts of their missions and the establishment of Buddhism on the island.
 
 
 
• **Pali Language**
 
 
• Pali is the liturgical language of Theravada Buddhism and was used to compose the early Buddhist scriptures.
 
• The Dipavamsa and Mahavamsa are significant historical texts written in Pali.
 
• Pali is closely related to Sanskrit and was widely used in ancient India and Sri Lanka.
